A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Scalable In-Context Q-Learning. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, algorithms, and appendices A–I support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original reinforcement-learning benchmark results, component ablations, OOD evaluations, stitching experiments, and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds offline evaluations, two additional environments, and loss-weight sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The world model, prompt construction, three-head transformer, expectile learning, and advantage-weighted policy extraction are retained. Equation (7) introduces explicit coefficients but uses (1,1,1) for the main experiments, matching v2’s objective; other weights are tested as ablations.

E1.justification: V3 adds sparse-reward, multi-step PickPlace manipulation and high-dimensional Humanoid-Dir control (Section 4.7 and Appendix C). It also adds testing with externally collected trajectories (Section 4.1), substantially broadening task requirements and test-input conditions beyond v2’s coverage.

E2.justification: The seven baselines remain UNICORN, DPT, AD, IDT, DICP, DIT, and IC-IQL, with unchanged membership in corresponding comparisons. The new complex-task comparison reuses all seven; the added offline comparison uses existing DPT and DIT baselines. DIT’s citation update does not establish a different evaluated method.

E3.justification: V3 adds a distinct offline evaluation using ten randomly sampled external trajectories per task, shared across compared methods, alongside the retained interactive few-shot protocol. It also introduces controlled loss-reweighting experiments and settings for the new tasks, including 800,000 Humanoid-Dir training steps. The offline-return calculation remains underspecified.

E4.justification: V3 adds focused checks of robustness to external behavior-policy trajectories and sensitivity to the three loss weights (Section 4.1 and Appendix H). Existing component, OOD, stitching, data-quality, visualization, and temperature/history-length analyses remain. V2’s appendix ablation curves are relocated to v3 Figure 3.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over ten trials, 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals, and standard errors. The new tables extend uncertainty reporting without documenting a changed run-count, seed, or statistical-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds offline returns in Table 2, complex-task results in Figure 7/Table 6, and loss-weight results in Table 13. New S-ICQL returns include 425.30±61.68 on PickPlace and 728.63±15.54 on Humanoid-Dir. Matched existing return tables retain their values; these additions are not same-setting performance improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem, assumptions, and learning equations retain their substance. Equation (3) explicitly substitutes the encoder output into the existing prediction-error objective, while Equation (7) makes the existing equal weighting explicit. Neither version provides theoretical results or proofs that are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introduction contributions, and main conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic programming, world-model prompts, scalability, and learning from suboptimal data. Additional experiments support those retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning robustness to external trajectories, applicability to harder tasks, and loss-weight sensitivity. Section 4.4 narrows its stitching interpretation from globally optimal to globally superior policies. Appendix A’s limitations remain unchanged; the conclusion adds proposed future use of the decoder for detecting distribution shifts.

D1.justification: Appendices C–F add environment descriptions, collection settings, and S-ICQL hyperparameters for PickPlace and Humanoid-Dir. Reported world-model training time changes from 0.2–2 to 1–2 hours, and transformer time from 1–12 to 2–22 hours. Hardware and code-access information remain unchanged; these ranges do not establish slower matched experiments.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 broaden background coverage with language/diffusion-model fine-tuning, meta-RL surveys, and methods including LLIRL, MAML, and MACAW. The substantive positioning against DIT and IC-IQL remains unchanged, so this expands context without revising the central novelty argument.

P1.justification: V3 expands the introduction and related-work opening, edits the stitching and conclusion prose, adds Section 4.7, and repurposes Appendix H. Author ordering, affiliations, correspondence information, conference headers, and acknowledgements are updated. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 redraws all three panels of the central method overview and substantially expands the experimental displays with Tables 2, 6, and 13 and Figure 7. It moves the existing appendix ablation plot into Section 4.2 and expands implementation tables for the new tasks. Other retained plots are principally relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the already extensive evaluation with harder tasks and controlled loss-weight analysis, while improving the method diagram and documenting new-task settings. These provide useful incremental evidence and guidance without changing the method or principal existing results. The added offline evaluation has limited evidential weight because Section 4.1 does not fully explain how its returns are computed.
